cases.rationale: King and bishop manoeuvres change the capture of the queenside pawns. White's rook pressures the a-file through different move orders with no own-pawn clearance in both.
Queen checks and the exact capture of c4 drive the main choices. A separate durable plan is uncertain.
Rf2 coordinates the queen and bishop for the king attack. The f-file is already clear of white pawns.
The queenside pawn push and the rook rotations on c8 and b8 define the alternatives.
Queen entry on f7 and checks matter alongside the two advanced white pawns. Black's rook does not gain a shared newly cleared file.
Re2+ preserves a forced checking resource for the draw. The independent positional value of the c-pawn in the other replies is uncertain.
Pushing e4 permits the bishop to take d2 after a forcing sequence. The pawn changes the centre in additional routes.
Black can play e5 directly or reorganise before deciding which central pawn to advance.
The f-pawn break and f-file matter. The immediate Rf3 activity occurs in one credible branch. Its continuation under another choice remains unclear.
Black's b-pawn and White's a-pawn create distinct promotion resources. The checking sequences determine which is realised first.
White's d4 and rook development can combine to clear the d-file. The parallel use after an alternative is uncertain in the supplied lines.
Repetition and voluntary continuation remain available. A sustained strategic consequence of the choice is uncertain.
h5 forces a choice about pawn cover while alternatives reposition knights and rooks. The new shared rook-file use is absent.
Rb8+ starts a close mating sequence with the rook and bishop.
Bc3 forces a minor-piece trade that creates the c-passer, and the queen then attacks g5 in multiple searched lines.
White must take the h-pawn without giving up the d-pawn for free. The remaining passed pawns and rook activity define the endgame.
Several choices develop White's rook on an already available f-file and use the h- and a-pawn structure.
dxc6 changes the knight and bishop tactics. In the strongest line and after bxc5, White's b-pawn leaves the file, and the rooks contest it with a different b-pawn blockade.
The concrete queen entry and captures on d6 matter. The queenside pawn plans give Black more than one durable continuation.
Both rook defences revolve around the d-passer and king activity. No new common rook-file clearance.
f3 attacks the knight and opens a concrete rook sacrifice on f8. The weaker choices settle into different rook and pawn structures.
En passant changes the checking sequence and converts an otherwise losing position. The positional part beyond the early exchanges is uncertain.
The tactical capture and the rook checks interact with the d- and h-pawns. The rook does not use the newly cleared d-file durably in both alternatives.
Rxd1+ prevents a concrete rook loss and the immediate recapture matters. A separate lasting structural factor is uncertain.
Underpromotion forces the recapture. The outside c-pawn survives in a number of these lines. The promotion routes largely converge before the strategic outcome.
